Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Digital revenue collection is actively in use. The HETRA e-Payment portal is the official online tax payment platform for Madagascar (e-hetra.impots.mg). By end-2021, World Bank-supported digital tax collection from SMEs in four regions had collected approximately $18 million. Mobile money platforms are used for synthetic tax payments in the informal economy. The 2025 mandatory e-invoicing system further strengthens revenue collection digitalization. The IMF has been monitoring domestic revenue mobilization as a key program indicator, with BFM providing monthly dashboards on tax and customs administration performance. Revenue collection digitalization is described as a priority in Madagascar's SNMGFP ten-year plan and IMF program conditionality.

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: Madagascar has an operational tax portal. The e-HETRA (e-hetra.impots.mg) is the official online e-filing and e-payment portal for Madagascar taxes operated by the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI). It supports online execution of tax payment orders and consultation of order history. The tele-declaration platform 'e-HETRA Declaration' is also operational. Additionally, Decree No. 2025-738 (July 2025) mandated a centralized e-invoicing platform for all taxpayers, managed by the Tax Administration. These systems together constitute a comprehensive digital tax portal.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: B2B digital payments are operational in Madagascar. Mobile money is used for business-to-business transactions, particularly between SMEs and suppliers. The 2025 mandatory e-invoicing decree (Decree No. 2025-738, July 2025) requires all B2B transactions to be processed through a centralized electronic invoicing platform, mandating digital payment traceability for all businesses. Orange Money Pro supports B2B payment management. RTGS handles high-value interbank B2B settlements. The e-invoicing rollout (phased over 6 months to 2 years by business size) will significantly expand mandated B2B digital payment infrastructure.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: G2P payments via digital channels have limited but active use in Madagascar. The Human Development Cash Transfer (TMDH/HDCT) program distributes payments via Airtel Money (~60% of beneficiaries) and cash (~40%). The World Bank Madagascar Financial Inclusion Project had a sub-component (1.1.1) for digitizing teachers' salaries and student grants; while this activity faced delays and was eventually cancelled/modified (as of 2022), digital civil servant salary payments are being explored. The e-Ariary pilot (May 2025) lists salary disbursements and social transfers as priority use cases. NGO-operated conditional cash transfers via mobile money are well-documented. Government G2P is partially deployed but not at scale for the core public payroll.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: P2B merchant payments are supported across Madagascar's mobile money networks. Orange Money launched 'Orange Money Pro' for merchants in March 2025, enabling QR code payments and remote payment links with over 10,000 downloads. MVola also supports merchant payments via its developer portal and QR codes. POS terminals exist though adoption is low outside Antananarivo. The e-Ariary CBDC pilot (May 2025) explicitly includes merchant payments as a primary use case, including market vendors. Despite widespread availability, merchant acceptance remains limited outside urban areas due to trust and infrastructure constraints.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: P2G digital payments have limited but active use. The HETRA e-Payment platform was implemented by the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) for secure online payment of taxes and duties, and a tele-declaration platform 'e-HETRA Declaration' is operational. With World Bank support, the Malagasy government developed a system allowing SMEs to pay taxes digitally across four regions, collecting approximately $18 million by end 2021. Madagascar's 2025 mandatory e-invoicing decree further expands P2G digital payments. Mobile money is used for synthetic tax payments in the informal economy. However, digital tax/fee payment is not yet universal—uptake remains partial and concentrated in urban/formal sector.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: P2P payments are fully operational in Madagascar. The three mobile money operators—Orange Money, Airtel Money, and MVola—all support person-to-person transfers. Full interoperability across all three networks has been live since 2016, making Madagascar the second country in Africa (after Tanzania) where all mobile money providers have fully interoperable P2P services. MVola has over 10 million customers and P2P transfers are described as the primary use case. In 2023, mobile money platforms facilitated nearly 342 million transactions totaling approximately $8.5 billion USD.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: The Banky Foiben'i Madagasikara (BFM, Central Bank of Madagascar) directly operates the national payment system. Its mandate under the 1994 BCM Status and the 2016 Law No. 2016-004 includes ensuring the proper functioning of the payments system. BFM directly operates RTGS clearing, oversees the retail payment infrastructure, licenses and supervises electronic money institutions, and is directly piloting and operating the e-Ariary CBDC. BFM also participates in governance of the national financial inclusion strategy. It is not merely a regulator; it is the direct operator of core payment infrastructure.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: A partial consumer protection framework exists for digital payments. Law 2016-056 on electronic money and electronic money institutions includes consumer protection provisions. The Microfinance Law (2017) also includes consumer protection clauses. Madagascar's NFIS 2018-2022 set consumer protection as Strategic Axis 1. A 'dispute mediator' or ombudsman entity has been discussed as a proposed mechanism to be housed at the central bank, but was not yet established as of the research period. The CMIL (data protection authority) is not yet fully operational. The AFI/BFM December 2025 workshop validated draft agent network regulations with consumer protection components. Overall, the framework is partial—legislation exists but enforcement mechanisms and dedicated financial consumer protection infrastructure remain incomplete.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Madagascar's Data Protection Law (No. 2014-038) does not set out any general or specific obligation to notify the CMIL or data subjects in the event of a data security breach. According to DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World guide: 'The Data Protection Law does not set out any general or specific obligation to notify the CMIL or the data subject in the event of a data security breach.' There is no mandatory breach notification requirement, though the law does require data security measures be implemented.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Madagascar has Law No. 2014-038 on the Protection of Personal Data, enacted December 2014, promulgated January 2015. This is a general data protection law inspired by the EU's Data Protection Directive (95/46/EC), establishing principles for collection, processing, storage, and transfer of personal data. It created the Commission Malagasy sur l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) as the enforcement body. In June 2024, Madagascar ratified the Malabo Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection. However, there are no specific payment data provisions—the law is general data protection legislation. The CMIL was only formally established by decree in December 2023 and is not yet fully operational.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: No regular public performance reporting for the payment system was found. The IMF 2025 Article IV consultation notes that the BFM provides monthly dashboards on key performance indicators of tax and customs administration as part of ECF program conditionality. BFM publishes annual reports but detailed payment system statistics (transaction volumes, uptime, etc.) are not published in a regular public format. The AfricaNenda SIIPS report covers Madagascar's mobile money data on an annual basis, but this is an external research publication rather than official system performance reporting by operators or regulators. The 2024 SIIPS consumer deck for Madagascar provides data on usage patterns but is not an official regulator report.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Pro-poor governance mechanisms exist but are partial. Madagascar has a National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS 2018-2022 and ongoing updates), a National Coordination of Inclusive Finance (CNFI) housed in the Treasury, and the e-Ariary CBDC is explicitly designed for rural and underserved communities. The Central Bank has been working with AFI on regulations to expand agent networks for last-mile access. However, there is no dedicated pro-poor governance body specifically for payment system oversight, and the NFIS target of 45% financial inclusion by 2022 was not met (41% still excluded as of 2025). Disability inclusion is being piloted but not yet systematized.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No evidence found that scheme rules for Madagascar's mobile money or payment systems are publicly available. The interoperability arrangements between mobile money operators (launched 2016) were commercially negotiated. BFM regulations on electronic money institutions (Law 2016-056) are on record but detailed scheme rules, participation conditions, and technical specifications for the interoperable mobile money system or the e-Ariary pilot are not published publicly. The IMF FSAP 2016 noted regulatory gaps and recommended drafting a national payment system law. No public scheme rules document was identified in research.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Active digital payment users are estimated at 20-49% of the adult population. The AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 Consumer Deck for Madagascar notes 54% of some demographic segments use digital payments daily, but overall adult population coverage is lower. IFC (2023) reports over a third of the population (approx. 33-37%) uses mobile money. The Nikulipe data cites 37% of adults over 15 use mobile money regularly. The FRED database shows 6.12 million active mobile money accounts in 2024 out of a total adult population of approximately 15-16 million, which is roughly 38-40%. Active accounts are distinct from registered accounts (20+ million registered). Cash still dominates, particularly in rural areas where 63% of the population lives.

Definition: Whether independent external audits of payment system security, operations, financial controls, and compliance are conducted by third-party auditors, and whether audit results or summaries are made public.
Comments: Private audits of payment system components exist but no public audits of the payment system as a whole were found. IFC partnered with BFM in 2023 on credit registry modernization with training/capacity building but no public audit of payment infrastructure. The IMF FSAP 2016 constituted an independent review of Madagascar's financial system including payment systems and recommended adopting a national payment system law and giving BCM oversight powers. Madagascar's Court of Accounts (Cour des Comptes/SAI) conducts financial and compliance audits of government entities (documented in TANTANA project reports for 2024), but these focus on government financial management rather than payment system performance specifically. No public audit report dedicated to the payment system was identified.

Definition: Whether digital payment systems and access points (apps, USSD, agents) are designed to accommodate persons with disabilities (visual, hearing, mobility, cognitive impairments), and disability-disaggregated coverage rates if data available.
Comments: No evidence of disability-specific access provisions in digital payment systems. Mobile money access in Madagascar is primarily via USSD and basic phones, which provides some accessibility for visually impaired users. However, no dedicated disability access features, standards, or policies for digital payment systems were identified. UNDP/UN Joint Programme social protection work (2020-2022) developed disability screening tools and disability grants as supplements to cash transfer programs, but these are for social protection delivery, not digital payment system design. The e-Ariary pilot documentation does not mention specific disability access features. Financial inclusion strategies do not specifically address disability access in digital payments.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Government payment digitization remains below 20% of overall government payments. The World Bank Madagascar Financial Inclusion Project set a target of 36,000 civil servants' salaries paid digitally (from a baseline of 0), but the main activity for digitizing FRAM teachers' salaries and student grants was cancelled in 2022 due to the government's decision to award that responsibility to the Postal Institution. The revised World Bank project focused on 'Digitalization of Treasury payment instruments' instead. G2P cash transfers (social protection programs) reach approximately 39,000-60,000 households with mixed digital/cash delivery. The e-Ariary pilot (May 2025) includes salary disbursements as a use case but is still in pilot. Government payroll digitization in Madagascar is nascent.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: No specific provisions for refugee or migrant access to digital payment systems were found. Mobile money registration in Madagascar requires a national ID card, which would exclude refugees and undocumented migrants. Madagascar's financial inclusion strategy focuses on the domestic unbanked population. A quarter of the adult population lacks formal ID, which is a barrier for Malagasy citizens themselves. UNHCR presence in Madagascar is minimal (Madagascar is not a major refugee destination). International remittance receipt is functional via mobile money (e.g., MVola's MFS Africa partnership), which benefits Malagasy diaspora sending money home, but this does not address migrant access within Madagascar. No refugee-specific mobile money scheme or simplified KYC for refugees was documented.
